executive_summary.headline: DEMO (synthetic data): Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates already return about 25% per container at current prices; Germany and the United Kingdom are the strongest expansion cases but depend on prices still to be confirmed.
paragraphs: This is a demonstration study built entirely on synthetic data to show what the toolkit produces. None of its figures describe a real market.

In the synthetic data, Egypt exported USD 45.6 million of frozen vegetables (HS 071080) in 2025, the latest complete year, growing 11.1% a year since 2022. It ranks 13th of 14 reporting exporters with a 1.96% world share, so there is room to grow in large importing markets where its presence is small.

At the client's current prices, Saudi Arabia returns a 25.0% margin per container and the United Arab Emirates 25.3%, both above the 18% target. For the four other selected markets no price was given, so the model shows the price needed to reach the target margin instead of a margin.
The planned 54 containers a year would recover the one-time entry cost within 2 months, provided the planned volumes and prices hold.
recommendations: Protect the Saudi Arabia business first: it is the largest current market, earns 25.0% per container and its freight rate is a firm quote.
Test prices in the United Kingdom and Germany: obtain two buyer price indications in each market and compare them with the required price in the financial case before committing volume.
Resolve the open data before quoting: the Netherlands duty rate, the Kuwait inland delivery cost, and the gap between Egypt's and the Netherlands' reported trade.
executive_summary.key_caveat: Margins for four of the six markets are required prices, not observed ones: they show what must be charged, not what buyers will pay.

paragraphs: The study covers one product line, HS 071080 (frozen vegetables not elsewhere specified), exported from Egypt. Trade data cover 2021 to 2026; 2026 is partial, so trends use 2022 to 2025.
Every commercial, freight and tariff figure carries its source and a tier. Modelled freight and tariffs marked 'verify' are estimates that must be checked before any price is quoted.
bullets: Trade flows: synthetic Comtrade-shaped data generated for this demonstration.
Freight: two client quotes, one rate tool result, one published rate and two modelled estimates.
Costs, prices and terms: the client's own figures as recorded at scoping.

paragraphs: Egypt's exports reached USD 45.6 million in 2025, up 11.1% a year since 2022. Saudi Arabia is the largest destination, followed by the United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.
bullets: The United Arab Emirates did not report its imports for 2025, so Egypt's figure for that market cannot be cross-checked.
The Netherlands reports receiving much less from Egypt than Egypt reports sending, which usually points to goods passing through Dutch ports to other buyers.

paragraphs: Reported world imports totalled USD 2,480 million in 2025. The United States is the largest importer with a 26.6% share, followed by Germany, the United Kingdom, France and the Netherlands.
Most of the large importing markets are in Europe and North America, where Egypt's current presence is small.
Egypt is a small supplier in the global ranking. In the markets it already serves it holds a meaningful share: 16.8% of Saudi Arabia's imports and 15.9% of Kuwait's.
bullets: In the United Kingdom and Germany, Egypt holds 1.3% and 0.2% of imports respectively: entry would mean taking share from established suppliers.

paragraphs: All six lanes use 40-foot reefer containers. Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have firm forwarder quotes; Germany and Kuwait rely on a distance-based estimate fitted to two published benchmarks, so their freight carries a wide range.
Duties are zero under a trade agreement for Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom in this demonstration; the Netherlands rate is still to be verified.
bullets: Kuwait: the inland delivery cost at destination is missing, so the buyer's landed cost there is not shown.
Each tariff should be re-checked for recent changes before a price is quoted.

paragraphs: Six markets were taken forward: four existing markets to defend (Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom) and two to expand (Germany and Kuwait).

partner_notes.SAU: Largest current market; firm freight quote; zero duty in this demonstration.
partner_notes.ARE: Second-largest destination but not scored, because it reported no imports for 2025.
partner_notes.NLD: Large market and likely a re-export hub; duty to be verified.
partner_notes.GBR: Large and growing market where Egypt is a small supplier.
partner_notes.DEU: Largest European market; freight is a modelled estimate.
partner_notes.KWT: Small market where Egypt is already a major supplier.

not_prioritised.reason: Largest importer, but no current presence and the longest lane; worth a separate study once European prices are tested.
A current core market, not selected for this demonstration round; it would be modelled the same way once the client confirms prices and payment terms.

paragraphs: At current prices Saudi Arabia earns USD 6,720 per container (25.0%) and the United Arab Emirates USD 6,991 (25.3%). Selling at CFR, the client pays freight to the destination port; the buyer pays duty and delivery from there.

For the other four markets the model reports the price needed for an 18% margin. In Germany the buyer's landed cost at that price would be about 7.8% above the average import price, which suggests the target is hard to reach there without lower freight.

partner_verdicts.ARE: Viable at current price; confirm the market size, since the partner does not report.
partner_verdicts.NLD: Required price shown; duty to be verified before quoting.
partner_verdicts.GBR: Required price lands close to the market's average import price; worth testing.
partner_verdicts.DEU: Required price lands above the market average; viable only with better freight or a premium position.
partner_verdicts.KWT: Required price shown; destination delivery cost still missing.

diagnostic: What do buyers in the United Kingdom and Germany pay today for comparable product?
Is the Netherlands gap explained by goods moving through Dutch ports to other markets?
macro: Freight on the modelled lanes can move well outside the estimated range.
Exchange-rate moves change the cost of goods in dollars; see the FX sensitivity in the workbook.
data_limits: All trade data in this demonstration are synthetic.
2026 is a partial year and is excluded from trends.

two_weeks: Request two buyer price indications each in the United Kingdom and Germany.
Verify the Netherlands duty rate and the Kuwait destination delivery cost.
thirty_days: Get forwarder quotes for the Germany and Kuwait lanes to replace the modelled freight.
Re-run the financial model with the confirmed prices and rates.
ninety_days: Ship a trial container to the best-scoring expansion market and record the actual landed cost.
